text:
- chief complaint: right knee pain after twisting the knee while falling from a ladder.
- history of present illness: the patient twisted the right knee while trying to catch a fall from a ladder yesterday. Pain persists despite ice and ibuprofen. Past history includes atrial fibrillation (on digoxin) and prior nose surgery.
- physical examination: tenderness over the medial meniscus, pain with knee flexion and twisting, mild pain with valgus stress, normal sensation, no calf pain. X-ray shows no fracture or dislocation, with small fluid.
- symptoms experienced by the patient: inner right knee pain, worse with bending and twisting.
- new medications prescribed or changed: ibuprofen (Motrin) 800 mg every six hours with food, two-week supply.
- follow-up instructions: knee brace and temporary crutches for a few days, return visit in about one week, MRI if not improved.

Note: the doctor's x-ray review mentions the left knee, but the rest of the visit refers to the right knee. Please verify laterality.
